budget_items.topic: 222 West Townsend Road - tax revenue if not acquired
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said that if the town does not exercise its right of first refusal, the parcel will be developed and return roughly the stated share of its taxable value to the tax rolls.

An Open Space Committee member said land in chapter 61A represents a real tax break the town gives up, describing it as the town shedding an amount of money each year, and argued decisions on right of first refusal should weigh that investment.

At the Montachusett Regional Planning Commission, budgeting for the coming year was discussed, and it was reported that EPA grants (e.g., for culverts) have been cancelled or put on indefinite hold federally.

decisions.decision: Two public information sessions on MBTA Communities Act zoning options were scheduled for June 11 at 9:30 a.m. and June 16 at 6:00 p.m., both at the Adult Activity Center (Eagle House), to be posted as board meetings.

After a tied vote for chair, the board decided to leave the chair position unchanged for now and revisit the reorganization vote at the June 23rd meeting, with the chair report item first on that agenda.

For 100 Townsend Harbor Road, the board decided to continue the hearing to June 23rd so the incoming interim planner could review the storm water submission, and asked the applicant to incorporate Graves' (peer reviewer) minor comments directly into revised plans before that meeting.
For 1083 Northfield Road, the board directed the applicant to obtain peer review of the revised (5-lot) plans and continued the hearing about a month to allow that.
The board chair said he would consult the town manager on whether/how the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum requirement could be legally reduced, before any vote to change it.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board held its annual reorganization, holding town elections for chair, vice chair, clerk and committee representative roles; the vote for chair between Matt Allison and Matt Brener ended in a tie twice and was left unresolved to be revisited at the next meeting, while other roles (vice chair, clerk, and various committee reps) were filled without contention. The board also held a joint session with the Open Space Committee on chapter 61A right-of-first-refusal process and voted, along with Open Space, to recommend the town not exercise its right of first refusal on 222 West Townsend Road. Three public hearings were held: 1083 Northfield Road (continued a month pending peer review of a revised 5-lot plan), 443 West Townsend Road lot 3 (approved with three bylaw waivers for a common driveway), and 100 Townsend Harbor Road (continued to June 23rd after abutters raised stormwater/lake concerns, pending review by the incoming interim planner).

what_happened.line: The Planning Board's chair election tied twice between Matt Allison and Matt Brener and was left unresolved, to be revisited June 23.
The board and the Open Space Committee both voted to recommend the town not exercise its right of first refusal on land at 222 West Townsend Road.
A special permit for a common driveway at 443 West Townsend Road lot 3 was approved with three bylaw waivers.
A stormwater permit hearing for 100 Townsend Harbor Road was continued to June 23 after abutters raised concerns about runoff into Hickory Hills Lake.
A hearing on a revised five-lot plan at 1083 Northfield Road was continued about a month pending peer review.

why_it_matters: The tied chair vote leaves the board without a settled leader going into its next meeting, though vice chair, clerk, and committee-representative seats were filled without contest.
Declining the town's right of first refusal on the West Townsend Road parcel means it can be sold and developed rather than held for conservation, adding it to the tax rolls instead.
Residents near Hickory Hills Lake get another chance to weigh in on stormwater runoff from the Townsend Harbor Road project before the board rules on the permit.
